name: OS desktop
source: A product told as an old computer desktop: windows open, stack and drag, dialogs ask questions, a cursor does the acting, in the conventions of Mac Classic, Windows 95 or a Y2K candy-glass desktop. Described from the atlas retro-OS entry; no vendor art, icons or sounds are carried.

frame_device.what: A full-frame desktop in one era (classic, win95 or y2k) with a wallpaper, a few desktop icons, a taskbar or menu bar and a cursor that is the film's actor.
frame_device.moves: The cursor travels and clicks; windows open from icons, drag, stack in cascades and close; a dialog interrupts with the beat's question and the cursor answers it.

ground_motion: The cursor idles with a pixel-step drift, a clock or a progress bar ticks in a window, the wallpaper may scroll a few pixels; nothing is frozen between clicks.

type.classes: The era's system face (a Chicago-like pixel face, a bitmap sans, or a rounded Y2K sans) at UI sizes, plus one display face for a title window.
type.behaviour: Text appears as typed (cursor + blink) or as window content that opens; dialog text is sentence case and fully readable at rest; the claim sits inside a dialog or a document window.

image.treatment: Flat era chrome (1-bit dither, bevels or candy glass) built in CSS; the product's real UI sits inside a window as a screen plate; generated art only as icons or wallpaper in the era's style.
image.behaviour: Windows pop or zoom-rect; the cursor moves in steps; no motion blur; classic uses wireframe zoom-rects, win95 uses instant pops, y2k uses bounce and gloss.

transitions: zoom-rect from an icon to a window (classic)
the screen shuts down to a dot or restarts to a boot screen
scene drags off in a window and the next window slides under it

techniques.name: Window open
techniques.what: A window opens from an icon with the era's own open move.
techniques.route: RasanRetroOS.open(tl, win, {at, duration: 0.4, from: iconBox}); classic = zoom-rect, win95/y2k = pop.

techniques.name: Cursor click
techniques.what: The cursor crosses the screen to a control and presses it.
techniques.route: RasanRetroOS.click(tl, cursor, target, {at, duration: 0.5}); cursor stepped: true for period hardware.

techniques.name: Window drag
techniques.what: The cursor grabs a title bar and carries the window to a new place.
techniques.route: RasanRetroOS.drag(tl, cursor, win, {at, duration: 0.8, to: [x, y]}); the window lands on top (zIndex set).

techniques.name: Window stack cascade
techniques.what: Five windows open in a cascade, each offset from the last, a pile of work.

techniques.name: Dialog question
techniques.what: A dialog asks the beat's question and the cursor clicks the answer.
techniques.route: RasanRetroOS.dialog(d, {title, text, buttons: ['Yes', 'No']}) opened with open(); click(tl, cursor, win.buttons[0]).

techniques.name: Typed document
techniques.what: A text window fills with typed lines at reading speed.
techniques.route: RasanTypeOnly or a char-by-char tl.set reveal on the window body at 14 cps with a blinking caret via tl.set every 0.5 s.

techniques.name: Era switch
techniques.what: The same desktop is re-skinned from one era to the next as the story moves through time.
techniques.route: Swap the desktop class (classic to win95 to y2k) with tl.set on a hard cut at a beat; same window content, new chrome.

techniques.name: Shutdown to a dot
techniques.what: The screen collapses to a bright dot and the film ends or restarts.
techniques.route: A full-frame black layer; scaleY 1 to 0.01 then scaleX to 0.01 over 0.3 s, power2.in; the dot fades 0.4 s later.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of a line enters from its own place and settles into the line with a lift; the key word last with a little more overshoot.
techniques.route: RasanShape.split(el, {by: 'words'}) on dialog and title text; each word from its own 20 to 60 px offset, 0.5 s, stagger 0.08 s; window text is typed instead.

signature: A dialog box carries the product claim, the cursor presses OK, and the desktop shuts down to a single dot.

density.note: A new window, click or dialog every 0.8 to 1.4 s; layers at the peak: 5 to 9 (wallpaper, icons, 2 to 4 windows, dialog, cursor).

palette.note: The era sets the palette (classic 1-bit, win95 teal and grey, y2k candy); a brand colour is the accent and the title-bar tint.

do: Pick one era per film (or one planned era switch)
Let the cursor be the actor and move it in steps
Keep dialog text fully readable at rest
Show the real product as a window screen plate
Build the chrome in CSS, not stock screenshots
dont: Do not copy a vendor's logos, icons or sounds
Do not mix three eras in one frame
Do not blur or glow the chrome
Do not skip the cursor; the film needs its actor
